Subject: SOC 2 Type II report + coverage clarification needed to finalize PO

Diego —

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement has one gating item before we can issue the PO: Accelerant requires a SOC 2 Type II report that covers the audit period Jan 1, 2026 — Dec 31, 2026. If you don’t have the full Type II report for that period, we will accept a formal bridge/interim attestation from your auditor that states coverage and any planned timeline to produce the full Type II.

Can you confirm by EOD Wednesday (Jun 2) whether Redwood can provide either: 1) the Type II report for 2026, or 2) an auditor-signed bridge letter and interim attestation with a committed delivery date for the full report?

We attached our questionnaire to this thread (Accelerant_Audit_Questions.xlsx) — it calls out specific controls we validate (change mgmt, access logs, incident response). We’ll also need a list of evidence you can share immediately for procurement/legal review.

We’re trying to close the PO next week; please treat this as high priority.

Thanks,
Rebecca
Procurement Manager, Accelerant Health

Subject: RE: SOC 2 Type II report + coverage clarification needed to finalize PO

Team —

Quick assessment: Redwood’s latest Type II audit window completed Feb 2027 (covers 2026 operations) but the formal report is not issued yet because the auditor sign-off process is still in review. That means we can:

- Provide an auditor-signed interim bridge letter confirming the testing window and that control testing was performed for Jan 1—Dec 31, 2026 (this requires an expedited sign-off request to the auditor).
- Or provide an internal interim attestation plus a commitment schedule for when the final Type II will be published (longer risk tolerance from buyer perspective).

To build either option we need to collect the following evidence immediately (I started a manifest): access logs (past 90 days), change management tickets and approvals for the production cluster, system configuration snapshots, incident response runbooks + last 12 months of incident summaries, and SOC testing matrices. I attached a lightweight manifest (SOC2-Evidence-Manifest.csv) with what we can reasonably produce in a 72-hour sprint.

Asking for help: I need legal to greenlight the auditor outreach (requesting a one-off accelerated sign-off) and Finance / Leadership to approve any incremental audit fees (if the auditor charges premium for an out-of-cycle sign-off). If we get approvals, Security can produce a bridge letter in ~48 hours. If we do internal-only attestation, we can produce a draft in ~24 hours but procurement may still push back.

Next steps I recommend:
- Diego: confirm buyer acceptance criteria (auditor-signed vs internal attestation).
- Marissa/legal: quick review and approval to contact auditor and sign fee agreement.
- Naomi/Monica: assemble evidence pack and upload to secured drive.

Attachment: SOC2-Evidence-Manifest.csv

All —

I reviewed the Accelerant questionnaire attached by Rebecca. The short list of artifacts they’ll want to see to accept a bridge/interim:
- Auditor bridge letter template (signed PDF)
- Evidence manifest: access logs, IAM config, MFA enrollment report, change mgmt approvals, configuration change history, disaster recovery test evidence, incident timeline docs, encryption-at-rest config screenshots, and a statement of scope for services.
- Snapshot of control testing (SOC testing matrix) and date ranges covered.

Operationally we can produce a bridge letter draft + internal attestation by Mon May 31 if Legal/Finance fast-track the auditor sign-off or accept internal attestation as temporary measure. I will coordinate the evidence sprint with Monica — we should start collecting logs and tickets now and stage them to a secure share (restricted).

If Finance confirms the auditor fee ok, I’ll reach out to our CPA partner and request an expedited signature on the bridge letter (48–72 hours depending on their availability).

Naomi
